facts.text: The on-road documents UN R131, UN R152, FMVSS No. 127, NHTSA New Car Assessment Program and Euro NCAP protocols do not regulate a quarry loader, haul truck, excavator or dozer merely because the machine has an automatic-braking function.
facts.quote: They do not regulate a quarry loader, haul truck, excavator or dozer because it has an automatic-braking function

facts.text: An on-road regulation or protocol should not be declared applicable to an off-road machine without an independent finding that the machine falls within its scope.
facts.quote: nothing should be declared applicable without an independent finding that the machine falls in their scope.

facts.text: UN R131, 02 series, covers heavy vehicles in categories M2, M3, N2 and N3.
facts.quote: UN R131, heavy vehicles (M2, M3, N2, N3), 02 series

facts.text: UN R131, 02 series, entered into force on 4 January 2023 and was published in EU OJ L 2025/1329.
facts.quote: in force 4 January 2023; published in EU OJ L 2025/1329

facts.text: UN R131 defines emergency braking as a demand from the AEBS to the service-braking system.
facts.quote: Emergency braking is a demand from the AEBS to the service-braking system.

facts.text: UN R131 requires a warning at least 0.8 seconds before emergency braking.
facts.quote: Warning at least 0.8 s before emergency braking

facts.text: UN R131 requires a braking demand of at least 4 m/s².
facts.quote: braking demand at least 4 m/s²

facts.text: UN R131 tabulates maximum impact speeds by vehicle category and test speed; for example, heavy hydraulic-brake trucks must achieve 0 km/h impact against a stationary target at test speeds up to 70 km/h.
facts.quote: maximum impact speeds tabulated by vehicle category and test speed (for example 0 km/h impact up to 70 km/h for heavy hydraulic-brake trucks against a stationary target)

facts.text: UN R131 specifies a child pedestrian target conforming to ISO 19206-2 crossing at 5 km/h.
facts.quote: child pedestrian target to ISO 19206-2 crossing at 5 km/h

facts.text: UN R131's false-reaction test requires passing between two stationary cars 4.5 m apart at 50 km/h without warning or braking.
facts.quote: a false-reaction test passing between two stationary cars 4.5 m apart at 50 km/h with no warning and no braking

facts.text: UN R131 requires a failure warning within 10 seconds.
facts.quote: failure warning within 10 s

facts.text: UN R131 permits no more than 10% failed runs per category in robustness testing.
facts.quote: no more than 10% failed runs per category in robustness testing.

facts.text: UN R152 Revision 2 / 02 series is a 2024 regulation for light vehicles in categories M1 and N1, published in EU OJ L 2024/2497.
facts.quote: UN R152, light vehicles (M1, N1), Revision 2 / 02 series** (2024; EU OJ L 2024/2497)

facts.text: UN R152 Revision 2 / 02 series is reported to use car-to-car tests at 10–60 km/h; these values were not verified against the primary text.
facts.quote: Car-to-car tests at 10 to 60 km/h

facts.text: UN R152 Revision 2 / 02 series is reported to use pedestrian tests at 20–60 km/h; these values were not verified against the primary text.
facts.quote: pedestrian tests at 20 to 60 km/h

facts.text: UN R152 Revision 2 / 02 series is reported to include false-reaction scenarios in which AEBS must not warn or brake; the passage cautions that the reported values were not verified against the primary text.
facts.quote: false-reaction scenarios in which the AEBS must not warn or brake. These values were not verified against the primary text.

facts.text: The FMVSS No. 127 final rule was issued on 9 May 2024, with a response to petitions on 26 November 2024.
facts.quote: final rule 9 May 2024; response to petitions 26 November 2024

facts.text: FMVSS No. 127 compliance begins on 1 September 2029.
facts.quote: compliance from 1 September 2029

facts.text: FMVSS No. 127 applies to US passenger cars and multipurpose vehicles, trucks and buses up to 4,536 kg GVWR.
facts.quote: applies to passenger cars and multipurpose vehicles, trucks and buses up to 4,536 kg GVWR

facts.text: FMVSS No. 127 requires no-contact avoidance of a lead vehicle up to 62 mph.
facts.quote: No-contact avoidance of a lead vehicle up to 62 mph

facts.text: FMVSS No. 127 requires pedestrian AEB in daylight and darkness.
facts.quote: pedestrian AEB in daylight and darkness

facts.text: FMVSS No. 127 requires forward-collision warning.
facts.quote: and forward-collision warning.

facts.text: FMVSS No. 127 false-activation tests use a steel trench plate at 80 km/h and a pass-through scenario; a test fails if peak deceleration exceeds manual braking by 0.25 g or more.
facts.quote: A false activation (steel trench plate at 80 km/h, and a pass-through scenario) fails if peak deceleration exceeds manual braking by 0.25 g or more.

facts.text: On 23 March 2026, the Department of Transportation told the D.C. Circuit it was preparing rulemaking to extend FMVSS No. 127 lead time by two years; the extension was a proposal, not adopted.
facts.quote: On 23 March 2026 the Department of Transportation told the D.C. Circuit it is preparing a rulemaking to extend lead time by two years (a proposal, not adopted).

facts.text: The NHTSA New Car Assessment Program final decision notice was signed in November 2024 and appeared in the Federal Register on 3 December 2024.
facts.quote: final decision notice signed November 2024, Federal Register 3 December 2024

facts.text: NHTSA New Car Assessment Program stationary and moving lead-vehicle tests start at 40 km/h and increase in 10 km/h steps to 80 km/h while no contact occurs; contact ends the test series.
facts.quote: Lead-vehicle stationary and moving tests start at 40 km/h and increase in 10 km/h steps to 80 km/h while no contact occurs; a contact ends that series.

facts.text: The NHTSA New Car Assessment Program lead-vehicle-decelerating test family uses headways of 12–40 m and target decelerations of 0.3–0.5 g.
facts.quote: The lead-vehicle-decelerating family uses headways of 12 to 40 m and target decelerations of 0.3 to 0.5 g.

facts.text: NHTSA New Car Assessment Program test values are consumer-assessment values, not law.
facts.quote: These are consumer-assessment values, not law.

facts.text: Within the Euro NCAP 2026–2028 protocols, the 2026 update is described as the largest overhaul since 2009.
facts.quote: The 2026 update is described as the largest overhaul since 2009

facts.text: The Euro NCAP 2026 update adds robustness testing with variations in speed and offset.
facts.quote: adding robustness testing with variations in speed and offset

facts.text: The Euro NCAP 2026 update adds virtual testing with spot checks.
facts.quote: and virtual testing with spot checks

facts.text: The Euro NCAP 2026 protocols contain more than 1,200 different test scenarios.
facts.quote: the 2026 protocols contain "more than 1,200 different test scenarios".

facts.text: Euro NCAP 2026–2028 pedestrian targets follow ISO 19206-2:2018.
facts.quote: Pedestrian targets follow ISO 19206-2:2018

facts.text: The Euro NCAP 2026–2028 bicyclist target follows ISO 19206-4:2020.
facts.quote: and the bicyclist target ISO 19206-4:2020.

facts.text: Euro NCAP 2026–2028 virtual-testing qualification matrices include stationary-target longitudinal cases at 10–50 km/h.
facts.quote: The virtual-testing qualification matrices include stationary-target longitudinal cases at 10 to 50 km/h

facts.text: Euro NCAP 2026–2028 virtual-testing qualification matrices include turning cases combining host speeds of 10–25 km/h with target speeds of 30–80 km/h.
facts.quote: turning cases combining host speeds of 10 to 25 km/h with target speeds of 30 to 80 km/h.

facts.text: An AB Dynamics engineer told Vehicle Dynamics International on 16 January 2026 that Euro NCAP considers a 20 km/h reduction in collision speed a pass for head-on scenarios CCFhos and CCFhol; this is vendor evidence.
facts.quote: For the head-on scenarios (CCFhos and CCFhol) an AB Dynamics engineer told Vehicle Dynamics International (16 January 2026) that "Euro NCAP considers a 20 km/h reduction in collision speed a pass"

facts.text: Euro NCAP is a consumer rating program, not a regulator, and its score is not regulatory evidence for any machine.
facts.quote: Euro NCAP is a consumer rating program, not a regulator; its score is not regulatory evidence for any machine.

facts.text: Expert opinion identifies transferable on-road scenario-space architecture as parametric description by ego speed, target speed, relative heading, lateral overlap, target class, visibility and lighting, braking capability and intervention timing.
facts.quote: Scenario-space architecture: parametric description by ego speed, target speed, relative heading, lateral overlap, target class, visibility and lighting, braking capability and intervention timing.

facts.text: Expert opinion recommends adapting the off-road scenario matrix to machine motion, object class, geometry, relative trajectory, payload, grade and friction, and sensor environment.
facts.quote: For the off-road system the matrix becomes machine motion, object class, geometry, relative trajectory, payload, grade and friction, and sensor environment.

facts.text: Expert opinion recommends transferring the ISO 19206 family's principle of standardised human and vehicle surrogates to off-road testing, but not using identical on-road targets.
facts.quote: Standardised human and vehicle surrogates as a principle (ISO 19206 family), but not the identical targets

facts.text: Expert opinion states that off-road test surrogates must represent persons in PPE, light vehicles under the nose of a haul truck, machines and fixed obstacles.
facts.quote: off-road surrogates must represent persons in PPE, light vehicles under the nose of a haul truck, machines and fixed obstacles

facts.text: Expert opinion states that off-road test surrogates must match camera appearance, radar cross-section, lidar reflectivity and ultrasonic response to each sensing modality.
facts.quote: with camera appearance, radar cross-section, lidar reflectivity and ultrasonic response matched to each sensing modality.
